transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Alex Kim (CSM), Mark Davis (Aurora), Sofia Martinez (Aurora Security), Liam O'Connor (Aurora Eng), Nina Patel (Aurora PM)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer, and Alex from customer success.
[00:08] Mark: Hi Jordan, thanks. We'll do quick intros — I'm Mark, lead on ML at Aurora, this is Sofia, handles security, Liam on infra, and Nina on the insurance product.
[00:17] Jordan: Great. The goal for today is to scope a POC — specifically the success criteria, the workload size so we can run realistic benchmarks, and to align on commercial guardrails: credits, pilot duration, and the procurement path.
[00:27] Priya: I'll run through our typical benchmark approach and the metrics we recommend collecting: p95 latency, throughput (qps), token cost, and qualitative quality checks against your sample prompts.
[00:36] Nina: Quick Q — we want to test both classification and a few generative flows for claim summarization. Expected traffic is low initially but latency sensitivity is moderate — claim triage should be <800ms p95 ideally.
[00:48] Liam: For infra, we want to know whether you recommend hosted or dedicated for the pilot — we prefer hosted to avoid procurement for now, but need assurances around data handling.
[01:02] Jordan: Hosted is typical for pilots. We can offer a scoped hosted pilot with VPC peering or private network tunnels if needed; we also include audit logs and optional KMS integration for keys. For commercial guardrails we usually offer a credits bucket plus a soft cap to avoid surprises.
[01:18] Sofia: Security question — will the pilot data be retained or deleted? We require short retention and auditability. SOC2 is a must.
[01:25] Alex: We have SOC2 in place; for pilots we can do customer-managed keys (KMS) and set retention to your policy — we'll put that in the pilot SOW.
[01:32] Mark: On success criteria — we want to (1) meet latency SLAs (p95 <800ms), (2) match or exceed current model accuracy on entity extraction (F1 within 3% of baseline), and (3) cost metrics: per-claim token cost below $0.XX — we'll provide baseline numbers.
[01:48] Priya: That makes sense. For F1 comparisons we usually run a blind evaluation set. For latency and cost we'll run both cold-start and warmed KV-cache runs to represent production.
[01:59] Priya: Can you share an initial QPS profile? Even ballpark helps size throughput.
[02:05] Liam: Right now it's about 5 QPS average with bursts up to 20 QPS during peak business hours; median request size is ~120 tokens, worst case 900 tokens for long summaries.
[02:19] Priya: Good — with that profile we'll recommend a hosted medium-sized pool for the pilot. For the benchmark harness we'll test sequence lengths at 120 and 900 tokens, and run sustained load to see throughput and p95.
[02:33] Jordan: On credits and pilot length, typical is a 4-week pilot with 1-2 months of optional extended testing. We can offer $15k of credits for the pilot and a soft cap at 120% usage, plus a checkpoint to decide on a dedicated or committed plan.
[02:48] Sofia: We need clarity on what the credits cover — inference only, or also support and extra services like security review?
[02:55] Jordan: Credits cover inference usage and basic onboarding support. Security review and SOC2 docs are shared at no cost. Professional services, deep integrations, or dedicated capacity are outside credits and priced separately; we'll note that in the SOW.
[03:08] Mark: Procurement note — our legal prefers a short pilot Order Form that avoids long contract terms. We'd like a path to procurement: if pilot passes, what's the next step?
[03:18] Alex: The common flow is pilot OF (order form) with statement of work and credits. If the pilot meets acceptance criteria, we'll present a commercial proposal for a committed Reserved Capacity or consumption contract, and our enterprise legal team will engage. We can provide a redlineable master subscription agreement.
[03:33] Nina: Timeline wise, we need to kick off before year-end — ideally bench runs in early December and a pilot run mid-December into January. Is that feasible?
[03:43] Priya: Yes, feasible. If you can provide sample data and QPS by Dec 2, we can prepare the harness and run baseline tests the week of Dec 8. Then pilot weeks follow.
[03:54] Liam: For the benchmarks please include cold start and warmed scenarios and a KV cache warmup plan, since our production will rely on prefix caching.
[04:03] Priya: We'll include KV cache warmup scripts and a runbook for how to interpret token counts with caching. We'll also provide a cost-estimation worksheet that maps tokens to credits.
[04:15] Mark: Can you also run a failure/reliability test — small percentage of faults and measure automatic fallback? That's a concern for us with critical claim automation.
[04:24] Jordan: Yes — Redwood's smart routing supports fallback to a smaller variant or standby region; we'll include a reliability test in the benchmark plan. For the pilot we can configure an automated fallback policy to simulate real-world degradation.
[04:36] Sofia: On compliance, we need to see encryption-at-rest details and the KMS flow. Also SSO/SAML and RBAC for team access.
[04:46] Alex: We'll share our security pack including encryption schemes, KMS integrations, SAML SSO docs, and audit log examples. For the pilot we can provide a scoped RBAC setup and one admin account for Aurora.
[04:58] Priya: A couple of technical notes — model variants: we suggest testing both a higher-quality/latency model and a faster quantized variant. That lets you measure the latency/quality tradeoff and cost delta.
[05:11] Mark: That aligns with our interests. We'll want concrete numbers: expected p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k requests for each variant.
[05:21] Priya: We'll produce a benchmark report with those columns and tie acceptance to the F1 metric and the p95 latency. Sample acceptance criteria line: "p95 latency <800ms AND F1 >= baseline-0.03 on the test set".
[05:36] Nina: Any standard commercial guardrails we should be aware of? For example, are credits refundable if pilot is canceled?
[05:43] Jordan: Credits are pre-purchased for the pilot period; unused credits can be reallocated to a follow-up pilot or applied to first month of committed usage within 60 days. Refunds are uncommon but can be discussed for exceptional circumstances.
[05:56] Mark: Pricing transparency is important. Can you share sample unit costs and an example invoice scenario for our estimated QPS?
[06:04] Jordan: Yes — we'll send a pricing worksheet with sample scenarios mapping tokens to credits and to dollars. That'll include example invoices for the pilot and for committed plans.
[06:13] Sofia: On data residency — we need EU data to stay in EU region for some customers. Is regional deployment possible for a pilot?
[06:20] Priya: Yes, we can route requests to EU region endpoints for the pilot; that does add latency for non-EU traffic but meets residency. We'll note region-specific performance in the benchmark.
[06:31] Liam: Regarding logs — we prefer log forwarding to our SIEM for the pilot. Is that supported?
[06:36] Alex: We support forwarding audit logs and traces to common SIEMs; we'll include a SIEM integration checklist.
[06:42] Mark: Great. Let's talk acceptance tests and sign-off. Who signs off — product or security?
[06:49] Nina: Product signs off on functional quality and metrics, security signs off on compliance items. We might require two sign-offs.
[06:56] Jordan: That's fine; we'll include a simple acceptance form that lists the pass/fail items for product and security. Once both sign, we move to procurement path.
[07:05] Priya: To summarize the technical POC plan: 1) baseline runs on your dataset, 2) synthetic load for QPS peaks, 3) KV-cache warmup and warmed runs, 4) fallback/reliability simulations, 5) quality evals (blind test set).
[07:18] Mark: Sounds good. Commercial guardrails: "4-week pilot, $15k credits, soft cap at 120%, credits apply to first committed invoice within 60 days, pilot OF with minimal terms" — tentative ok.
[07:33] Sofia: We'll need the security pack and example OF to legal early.
[07:38] Jordan: We'll send both in the next 48 hours.
[07:42] Alex: I'll prepare the onboarding checklist and kickoff agenda.
[07:45] Mark: One last Q — can we include a short SLA for pilot availability? Not enterprise SLA but an uptime target for the hosted pilot.
[07:53] Jordan: For hosted pilots we commit to 99% availability and will report incidents; enterprise SLAs are available for dedicated/committed customers. We'll include a statement in the OF.
[08:05] Nina: OK, let's capture action items and dates.
[08:10] Jordan: (recap) Jordan to send pricing and credits worksheet by Nov 27, Priya to share benchmark harness by Nov 26, Liam to supply datasets and traffic profile by Dec 2, Sofia to confirm SOC2/KMS needs by Dec 1, Alex to prepare kickoff agenda by Nov 28.
[08:29] Mark: Thanks all. We'll aim to have the sample data ready on Dec 2.
[08:33] Jordan: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pilot Order Form and security pack.
[08:38] Sofia: Thank you.
[08:40] End of call.
